search_strategy: Methodical and broad, but keyword-search-led rather than exhaustive enumeration. Wiki: ran a handful of /api/search keyword passes (ModelPrice, batch_rate, output_price_inferred, price_unavailable_reason, register_price, completion_window, litellm+model_cost, kluster, inference.net, unpriced) and then fetched ~8 specific page IDs whole via a home-written bs.py script that also dumps comments (pages 132, 139, 140, 142, 164 confirmed fetched). This caught every comment-only clue that happened to sit on a page whose body ALSO matched a search term (l5, l8, s3-l2), but missed comment-only clues on pages whose title/body never matched a search term (l2, l12, s1-l4, s2-l3) -- exactly the BookStack comment-blindness the ticket warns about -- and even missed the one page-BODY clue (s4-l2, 'weekly-sync-notes-week-of-jun-23-batch-mode') that WAS search-indexed, simply because none of the keyword passes matched it. Chat: dumped all 11 channels to local files via the Mattermost API (pipeline 2025, engineering 2474, code-review 3200 posts, etc.) and then grepped repeatedly for domain terms (resolve_model_price, batch_multiplier, unknown_window, star entry, asterisk, canonical/consolidat/unified). Full context was read with sed for every grep hit the agent followed up on -- both herring-reversal exchanges (rev1, rev2), the WS-050-adjacent 0.5/azure exchange, and the star-entry/unknown_window exchanges were all read as complete 6-9 line conversations. But two broad, unfollowed grep dumps ('ModelPrice'/'pricing'/'price' searches, lines 2480-2601) surfaced many remarks (s1-l1, l6, l11, l14, s1-l3, s2-l1, s3-l1) only as single out-of-context lines from Mattermost's search-snippet API, several of which were never revisited with a full sed read -- these produced the 'partial' and a few 'no' rows above. Mail: dumped the entire admin mailbox over IMAP (127 messages) to one file and read every relevant thread by line range in full, catching all 6 mail clues except one where the agent's own terminal truncated a message at a 10000-byte output cap.
end_reason: Not applicable -- the run completed normally: code was pushed, CI went green, and the release picked it up (provenance.pushed=1, provenance.ci_green=1, provenance.deployed=1). The only lost fact (g6.r1.observability) failed on a genuine implementation bug in the shipped code, not an infra or process failure.
notable: Task-version corpus divergence (line ~3892-3916): the mail thread 'Re: Weekly update: week of Apr 7' (g6.r2.g6r2-s2-l4) reads OPPOSITELY between this run's v6 world and the repo's v7 answer key. In the transcript, Konrad's final reply says the klusterai halving is WRONG ('it will have to go back up to the table rate... I had it the right way round after all'), correctly matching the true rule that klusterai must not be discounted. The v7 answer key instead quotes Konrad accepting the halved figure as correct, which would contradict the actual rule. Per instructions this is judged against what the transcript showed, and in this instance the v6 world happened to be the more internally-consistent version.

That same mail thread's middle message (Emil's reasoning, MSG 112) was cut by the agent's own '[... output limited to 10000 bytes; interior bytes omitted ...]' truncation notice -- a self-inflicted near-miss from reading too wide a sed range at once, not a search failure. It did not cost anything since rev1/rev2/g6r2-s2-l2 independently established the same conclusion.

The one lost fact (g6.r1.observability) is a clean implementation_slip: the agent wrote the correct catch-UnpricedModelError-and-degrade pattern twice (both status trackers, lines 5284-5299 and 5388-5402) but never applied it to the two external cost-processor overrides (_KlusterAICostProcessor, _InferenceNetCostProcessor) that call resolve_model_price indirectly through _register_external_model (lines 5076-5112) -- and never tested that specific path before calling the ticket done.

Five wiki-comment clues (g6.r1.l2, g6.r1.l12, g6.r2.g6r2-s1-l4, g6.r2.g6r2-s2-l3) plus one page-body clue (g6.r2.g6r2-s4-l2) were never fetched at all; none of this affected the final score because every fact they carried was independently supplied by other, found remarks -- the run's 33-remark redundancy (>=2 sources/3 weeks/2 channels per requirement) did its job.
